title: Signing a confidentiality agreement

items.title: What counts as confidential is defined
items.look_for: A definition of confidential information, and whether it must be marked
items.why_it_matters: An unlimited definition can cover things you already knew
items.question_to_ask: Does this cover information I already had?

items.title: The usual exceptions are present
items.look_for: Exceptions for public information, information you already had, and independent development
items.why_it_matters: Without them you can be held to secrecy over public facts
items.question_to_ask: Can we add the standard exceptions for public and pre-existing information?

items.title: Whether obligations run both ways is clear
items.look_for: Whether both sides or only one side is bound
items.why_it_matters: A one-way agreement protects only the other side

items.title: The confidentiality period is limited
items.look_for: How long the obligation lasts after the agreement ends
items.why_it_matters: A perpetual obligation is hard to comply with and hard to escape
items.question_to_ask: How long does this last after we stop working together?

items.title: The permitted purpose is defined
items.look_for: What you may use the information for
items.why_it_matters: It sets the boundary between use and misuse
items.question_to_ask: What may I use this information for?

items.title: Disclosure to your own team is allowed
items.look_for: Permission to share with employees or advisers who need to know
items.why_it_matters: Without it, ordinary work becomes a breach
items.question_to_ask: May I share this with my team and my accountant?

items.title: Disclosure required by law is carved out
items.look_for: Permission to disclose when compelled by law or a court
items.why_it_matters: You cannot contract out of a legal obligation
items.question_to_ask: What do I do if I am legally required to disclose?

items.title: What happens at the end is stated
items.look_for: A duty to return or destroy material, and any retention for records
items.question_to_ask: Can I keep one copy for my records and for backups?

items.title: Any pre-set penalty is reasonable
items.look_for: A fixed sum payable on breach
items.why_it_matters: A large fixed penalty raises the stakes of an accidental slip

items.title: No rights are transferred by accident
items.look_for: Wording that no intellectual property or licence passes
items.why_it_matters: Sharing information should not transfer ownership
items.question_to_ask: Does this give either of us rights over the other's work?

items.title: Where disputes are heard is stated
items.look_for: A named city, court or arbitration process
items.why_it_matters: A distant forum makes enforcement costly for both sides
items.question_to_ask: Where would a dispute be heard?

suggested_questions: How long does the confidentiality obligation last?
Does this cover information I already had?
Can I share this with my own team?
What do I have to do with the material at the end?

scenarios.title: I share information with a colleague by mistake
A court orders me to disclose
My team builds something similar independently

facts_to_have_ready: When you signed and what information was shared
Who on your side has seen the information
Whether the same information was available publicly
What you have been asked to stop doing
documents_to_bring: Emails showing what was shared and when
